title: Windows Loudness Equalization, reverse-engineered and ported to PipeWire
why_read: A reverse-engineering writeup porting a specific Windows audio feature to Linux's PipeWire is a solid, concrete systems-level project of interest to audio and OS enthusiasts.
analysis: Windows Loudness Equalization is an audio normalization feature, and reverse-engineering it to work on Linux's PipeWire sound server is a nontrivial technical undertaking. This kind of work typically involves analyzing audio DSP algorithms and reimplementing them without original source code or documentation. It's a niche but genuinely technical contribution that benefits Linux desktop audio quality. The decent engagement suggests both audio engineers and Linux desktop users find it valuable.
